# How to Use Google's New Gemini Features to Organize Your Busy Life

> **In short:** Gemini can now search across your Gmail, Drive, and Calendar in one question, and you can talk to it by voice or upload a photo. Connect your apps in the Gemini settings, then ask plain-English questions like "what's due this week?" to cut your admin time.

Picture Sunday afternoon: the kids' swimming reminders are buried somewhere in Gmail, the electric bill is hiding in a different email thread, and you've got a flyer photo on your phone you keep meaning to type into your calendar. Gemini — Google's AI assistant that lives inside your Google account — can pull all of that together if you set it up right. Here's how.

## What you'll need before you start

- A free Google account (the same one you use for Gmail). Sign-in is automatic if you're on Chrome.
- The **Gemini app** on your phone (free on iOS and Android), **or** open **gemini.google.com** in any browser on your computer.
- For Gemini to actually read your emails, you need to **connect Gmail in Gemini's settings** — Google will ask you to confirm which data the assistant can see. This is a one-time toggle.
- A phone with iOS 16+ or Android 10+ for the app, and a working microphone if you want to use voice.
- Some features are sharper on **Google AI Pro** (the paid tier, around $30 AUD a month at the time of writing), but the basics below work on the free plan.

## Step 1 — Open Gemini and sign in

Tap the Gemini app icon on your phone, or visit **gemini.google.com** on your computer. If you're not already signed in, tap **Sign in** and pick the Google account that holds your Gmail and Calendar. You'll see a blank chat box with a small microphone icon on the right and a paperclip on the left.

You'll know it worked when you see your Google account profile picture in the top corner and a "Hello" greeting from Gemini in the chat area.

💬 Example line: just type *"Hi"* to start — Gemini will respond and you'll know you're in.

## Step 2 — Connect your Gmail, Drive, and Calendar

In the Gemini app, tap your **profile picture** (top right) → **Settings** → **Connected apps** (sometimes labeled **Extensions**). On the website, click the **Settings** cog, then **Extensions**. Toggle on **Gmail**, **Google Drive**, and **Google Calendar**. Google will pop up a permissions screen — tap **Allow** on each one.

You'll know it worked when each app shows a blue "Connected" tick and the toggle stays blue when you leave and return to the page.

💬 Example line: a permissions request will read roughly *"Allow Gemini to read, compose, and send email on your behalf?"* — tap **Allow** if you're happy for it to read your inbox.

## Step 3 — Ask your first cross-app question

Now ask something Gemini actually has to dig for. In the chat box, type a single question that spans two apps. For example: *"Look in my Gmail for the kids' swimming lesson schedule, then check my Calendar and tell me if there's a clash next Tuesday."* Press **Enter**. Gemini will think for a few seconds, then show a short answer with little source chips (small clickable labels) underneath — tap one to jump straight to the email.

You'll know it worked when you see source chips linking back to a specific Gmail message and a Calendar entry under the answer.

💬 Example line: *"Find my latest electricity bill in Gmail. Who is the provider, how much is due, and when?"*

## Step 4 — Try a voice conversation with Gemini Live

In the Gemini app, tap the **waveform icon** (the squiggly line, top right of the chat box) — this opens **Gemini Live**, the back-and-forth voice mode. Speak normally, as if talking to a person. You can interrupt Gemini mid-answer, and it will adjust. On the website, click the **microphone** in the chat box for a simpler one-shot voice reply.

You'll know it worked when the waveform icon turns into a colored pulsing circle and Gemini replies out loud in a natural voice.

💬 Example line: speak out loud: *"I have chicken, a capsicum, and some yoghurt. What's for dinner, and what's on the shopping list?"*

## Step 5 — Upload a photo or screenshot for a calendar event

Tap the **paperclip** (or **+** icon) in the chat box and choose **Photos** or **Files**. Pick the screenshot of the school newsletter or the photo you took of the flyer. Then type: *"Read this and add the events to my Calendar."* Gemini will pull out the dates, times, and event names, and show a draft entry before it saves anything.

You'll know it worked when you see a preview card with the event title, date, and a green **Add to Calendar** button.

💬 Example line: *"Extract the dates from this flyer and add them as all-day events on the right days."*

## Step 6 — Use Gemini inside Gmail itself

Open Gmail on the web (or the app) and look for the **"Ask Gemini"** button — it's a small four-point star icon, top right of an open email, or open the side panel from the toolbar. Click it and ask things like *"Summarize this long email chain"* or *"Draft a polite reply saying I'll pay on Friday."* It's the same AI, just sitting inside Gmail so you don't have to switch tabs.

You'll know it worked when you see a short summary in the side panel, or a draft reply appears in the reply box ready to edit.

💬 Example line: *"Write a reply to this. Keep it short, polite, and say I'll pay the bill on Friday."*

## Common mistakes

- **Forgetting to connect the apps.** If Gemini keeps saying "I can't access your emails," go back to **Settings → Connected apps** and check Gmail is toggled on. Without that step, it only knows what you type into the chat.
- **Asking questions that are too broad.** "Tell me about my life" gets a vague answer. Narrow it down: *one app, one time window, one job* — like "Find my tax documents from July in Drive."
- **Treating every answer as gospel.** Gemini can still get dates or amounts wrong. Always tap the source chip and read the original email before you act on a number.
- **Leaving voice mode on by accident.** If your phone battery drains fast, check that Gemini Live isn't still running in the background — swipe it away from your recent apps when you're done.

## What this means for you

- **For your home admin:** Use Steps 3 and 5 to clear Sunday-evening admin — find bills, add school dates, and draft replies in one sitting instead of hopping between five apps.
- **For work or a side hustle:** Step 6 inside Gmail is the quickest win. Summarize long client threads and draft replies in your own tone, then edit before sending.
- **If you've never used AI before:** Just do Steps 1, 2, and 3 today. That alone replaces about half an hour of inbox digging every week.

Try one question today — even something as small as "what's in my calendar tomorrow?" — and you'll feel the difference within a minute.
